payment-verification-desk-card.pdf: CyberSafe SME Nigeria Practical cybersecurity guidance for Nigerian SMEs Free educational resource | Keep completed forms private | 1 PAYMENT VERIFICATION DESK CARD Stop. Check. Confirm. For shop counters, payment desks and staff approving transfers. MONEY COMING IN: Before you release goods or complete an order 1. Check your own trusted banking channel. Open the business bank app or another reliable bank-approved account view yourself. Do not accept a screenshot, SMS or customer alert as proof of cleared funds. 2. Match the details. Check the amount and relevant payment details against the order. If pending or unclear, wait and verify with the bank. 3. Use one agreed decision-maker. Staff should know who is authorised to confirm payment. 4. If not confirmed, do not release goods yet. Explain that the order can be released after payment confirmation. MONEY GOING OUT: Before you pay a supplier or contractor 1. Check the request against the expected invoice/order. 2. If supplier details change, use a previously trusted telephone number to confirm; never rely on the contact in the change message. 3. Check beneficiary details on the transfer screen. 4. Follow your approval rule; higher-value payments may require a second authorised check. 5. Keep payment evidence in approved secure records. Your business rules: Person/role who confirms incoming credits: ________ Person/role approving transfers: ________ Second approval above: NGN ________ Known internal contact for payment questions: ____________________ Suspected fraud? Contact your bank/payment provider immediately via its official channel. Preserve evidence. No recovery guarantee. Never disclose OTPs, PINs, passwords or card security codes. Learn: /protect-your-business/payment-security · /threats/fake-bank-alerts
suspicious-message-staff-card.pdf: CyberSafe SME Nigeria Practical cybersecurity guidance for Nigerian SMEs Free educational resource | Keep completed forms private | 1 SUSPICIOUS MESSAGE STAFF CARD Pause. Check. Report. For business WhatsApp, SMS, email and social-media messages. PAUSE Look for requests for passwords, OTPs or PINs; sudden payment urgency; secrecy; unexpected links; or familiar names making unusual demands. Familiar photos and display names do not prove identity. CHECK Use a separate trusted route: call a saved number or independently open the official app. Verify the request, not only the sender; a genuine contact might have a compromised account. Never share a login code. Suggested reply: “I will confirm this through our usual contact details before taking action.” REPORT Tell your supervisor or account owner promptly. Preserve messages safely; do not forward to unrelated groups. If you clicked, shared credentials or sent money, report immediately and contact the affected provider or bank. Team contact for suspicious requests: ______________________________ Remember: asking for a second check is responsible. Learn: /threats/phishing · /threats/social-engineering
